newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds up, cheered by unchanged German repo.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds up, cheered by unchanged German repo.

text.p: Danish bond prices climbed moderately on Tuesday in a market encouraged by the German Bundesbank's decision not to change repo rates, with dealers confident that FOMC would leave U.S. rates the same.
"Market jitters about a hike of German repo rates have evaporated and nobody expects any adjustment at the FOMC meeting," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.20 point from the opening at 112.73, yielding 6.08 percent. The seven percent 2007 state bond, due to be benchmark on September 1, rose 0.21 point to 105.63, with yield at 6.27 percent.
Turnover in the tone-setting 2006 and 2007 papers was 400 million and 1.4 billion crowns respectively.

The 2006's September future was untraded at 112.32, while the six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.27 point to 91.50. The crown traded at a stable 3.8083 per mark at 1100 gmt. The 10-year yield gap with Germany widened one basis point to 63 since Monday afternoon.
The Central Bank was active on the market selling a total of 800 million crowns worth of assorted bonds as part of its routine financing operations.
